Reset your position before the next rep, or keep the same position if you are holding for time.
tips: Keep the dumbbell close and shorten the leg extension if your lower back takes over.
Keep the movement controlled, breathe steadily, and stop or regress the exercise if you feel sharp pain or lose form.

items.description: Hold a backpack high against your chest while performing a controlled squat.

images.alt: Adult standing on a mat holding a closed backpack high against the chest with feet grounded and trunk lightly braced.
Adult holding a backpack high against the chest in the bottom of a controlled squat with chest tall, knees tracking, and heels down.
Adult standing tall after the squat with the backpack held high, feet planted, and posture reset before the next repetition.

items.name: Backpack Front Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Load the backpack lightly, close all zippers, and hold or wear it securely before the first rep.
Hold a backpack high against your chest while performing a controlled squat.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a light load first and make sure lids, straps, and zippers are secure.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Cradle a backpack in the crooks of your elbows and squat with an upright torso.

images.alt: An adult stands on a mat with feet hip-to-shoulder width, bracing lightly while checking a closed backpack before the squat.
An adult cradles a backpack evenly in the crooks of the elbows with a tall chest and planted feet.
An adult lowers into a backpack Zercher squat with knees tracking over the feet, heels grounded, and the backpack held securely.
An adult stands tall from the squat while keeping the backpack cradled, pressing through the whole foot before resetting.

items.name: Backpack Zercher Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Load the backpack lightly, close all zippers, and hold or wear it securely before the first rep.
Cradle a backpack in the crooks of your elbows and squat with an upright torso.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a light load first and make sure lids, straps, and zippers are secure.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Use a wall for light balance support while holding the bottom of a squat.

images.alt: Adult standing with their back lightly against a wall, feet stepped forward on a mat, with callouts for chest position, wall contact, and foot placement.
Adult sliding down the wall into a supported squat with feet flat, a downward motion arrow, and callouts for knee tracking and heel contact.
Adult holding a beginner wall-supported squat with back against the wall, knees bent over feet, and callouts for chest position, knee tracking, and whole-foot pressure.

items.name: Wall-Supported Squat Hold
steps: Stand with your back against a wall and feet a comfortable step forward.
Slide down until your knees and hips are bent to a manageable angle.
Use a wall for light balance support while holding the bottom of a squat.
Hold or move as prescribed, then press through your feet and slide back up the wall.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Stand close enough to control the movement without jamming your wrists, shoulders, or back.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Hold a backpack at the chest and lower slowly until you tap a chair.

images.alt: Adult stands in front of a sturdy chair holding a backpack at the chest with feet planted on a mat.
Adult lowers slowly into a goblet squat with hips reaching back toward the chair, knees tracking toes, and heels down.
Adult stands tall again from the chair squat while holding the backpack close and pressing through the floor.

items.name: Slow Goblet Squat to Chair
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart.
Hold a backpack at the chest and lower slowly until you tap a chair.
Reach your hips back and lower until you lightly touch or hover above the chair.
Press through the floor to stand tall without rocking forward for momentum.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Use only a stable surface that will not slide, tip, or open unexpectedly.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Place one foot slightly behind the other so the front leg does more work during the squat.

images.alt: Adult stands barefoot on a mat in a short staggered stance with one foot slightly behind the other and callouts for stance, bracing, and grounded feet.
Adult lowers into a staggered-stance squat with both heels down, hips back, and a knee-tracking callout.
Adult stands tall in the same staggered stance with an upward arrow showing the press through the foot to reset.

items.name: Staggered-Stance Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.
Start with enough open floor space to move comfortably.
Place one foot slightly behind the other so the front leg does more work during the squat.
Bend your hips and knees to lower under control while your heels stay grounded.
Press through your whole foot to stand tall and reset before the next rep.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, or joint pinching.

items.description: Use a split stance with the front heel slightly elevated to bias the front thigh.

images.alt: Adult in a split stance with the front heel supported on a low wedge and the rear foot behind, torso upright.
Adult lowering into a heel-elevated split-stance squat with the front knee tracking over toes and the heel supported.
Adult in the bottom position of a heel-elevated split-stance squat with whole-foot pressure and knee tracking cued.

items.name: Split-Stance Heel-Elevated Squat
steps: Stand with feet about hip-to-shoulder width apart and brace lightly through your trunk.

items.name: Surrender Lunge
steps: Start kneeling on a mat with your torso tall.
Step one foot forward into a half-kneeling lunge.
Press through the front foot to stand up, bringing the back foot forward.
Reverse the motion carefully back to kneeling, then repeat or switch lead legs.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Skater Step-Back
steps: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and a little space around you.
Brace lightly and begin the movement slowly so you understand the range.
Step diagonally back like a skater and tap the rear foot lightly.

items.name: Split Lunge Jump
steps: Stand tall with feet under hips and brace your trunk.
Step into the lunge with one foot and lower until both knees bend comfortably.
Keep the front knee tracking over the middle toes and your torso controlled.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.
Add a small hop only after you stand tall, then land softly and reset.
tips: Keep knees tracking the same direction as your toes.
Use your whole foot instead of rolling onto toes or collapsing arches.
Choose a range where you can keep control and balance.
Land with soft knees and stop plyometric reps before landings get loud or stiff.
Move under control, breathe steadily, and stop if you feel sharp pain, numbness, or joint pinching.

items.name: Tree Pose Toe Stand

Keep ankles roughly in line with knees if possible and support yourself on hands or forearms.
Rock hips gently back and forward or hold the position as listed.
Come out slowly by bringing knees back under hips.
tips: Keep the stretch in the hip or glute, not the knee.
Use hands, pillows, wall, or chair support to make the position easier.
Keep pelvis controlled instead of twisting to chase range.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.

steps: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and a little space around you. Set up your wall or chair before you start and make sure it will not slide or tip.
Use a wall, chair, or floor for balance if listed.
Move the leg or knee through the listed swing, circle, slide, or curl pattern.
Stay within a smooth range instead of forcing height.
Repeat and switch sides.
tips: Keep knee and toes pointing in the same general direction.
Use a soft bend in the knee when a straight-leg stretch feels too intense.
Ease in gradually; do not bounce into hamstring, calf, or groin stretches.
For dynamic mobility, stay smooth and controlled instead of forcing maximum range.
A good stretch feels like mild to moderate tension, not sharp pain.
